headline: Africa's Richest Man Funds $660M Pipeline to Speed Up Fuel Across East Africa
meta_description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote is helping fund a new fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti, expected to cut fuel transport time from 5 days to just 1.
summary_short: A $660m fuel pipeline between Djibouti and Ethiopia will slash transport times and strengthen energy security for the landlocked nation.
body:
Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote is backing construction of a $660 million fuel pipeline that will reshape how petroleum products reach Ethiopia's interior. The 120-kilometer line will connect the port city of Djibouti to a distribution hub in Dewele, Ethiopia, with storage for about 400 million litres. Most remarkably, it will shrink fuel delivery time to Addis Ababa from five days to just one—a transformation that matters enormously for a landlocked nation dependent on Djibouti's port for critical imports. Operations are expected to begin within 18 months.

The project addresses a genuine bottleneck in East Africa's supply chain. By accelerating petroleum delivery, the pipeline will ease pressure on transport networks that currently support aviation, agriculture, construction, and other industries. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has emphasized the infrastructure's role in strengthening the nation's energy security. Djibouti stands to gain as well, through increased port activity, job creation, and higher government revenues.

Dangote's involvement reflects his broader vision of expanding African infrastructure and manufacturing capacity. His cement company operates at 55 million tonnes annual capacity across the continent, while his Nigerian oil refinery currently processes 700,000 barrels daily and aims to double that capacity. The refinery recently raised $1.63 billion through a stock exchange listing. Looking ahead, Dangote's company is preparing to break ground on a new 700,000-barrel-per-day crude oil refinery in Kenya's Lamu region. These interconnected projects reveal a strategy to build resilient energy and industrial systems across Africa—moving beyond extraction toward integrated regional infrastructure.
quick_facts: $660 million fuel pipeline connecting Djibouti port to Ethiopia
Reduces fuel transport time from 5 days to 1 day
120-kilometer pipeline with 400 million litre storage capacity
Backed by billionaire Aliko Dangote, Africa's richest person
